messages:
michael: Hey team — quick benefit question for a hire who came through an EOR (GlobalHire) and then converted to direct Redwood payroll on 2025-04-15. Do we treat their original EOR start date (2025-01-06) as their Redwood service date for 401(k) eligibility, employer match proration, and vesting? Also: can prior contributions made via GlobalHire be transferred into our 401(k) and can we do retroactive employer match for Jan–Apr?

sarah: @michael good Q. Short answer: it depends on vendor & payroll rules. Longer: eligibility & match proration usually follow "first day of service" if we formally recognize the EOR period as continuous service — but we need records from GlobalHire + fidelity/vendor confirmation. Vesting schedules are tied to credited service; if we accept the EOR time as credited, vesting can be backdated.

ben-payroll: FYI payroll constraints: we can process retro employer contributions, but vendor cutoffs matter. Some vendors allow backdated employer contributions only up to the plan year or a vendor-specific window (often 60–90 days). Need case opened with vendor to confirm.

sam: Steps I recommend: 1) michael, confirm employee name + EOR start/end + direct hire date. 2) ask GlobalHire for contribution history/export (dates/amounts). 3) benefits@redwood.com will open a transfer case with Fidelity (or our 401k provider) to accept rollover/transfer and confirm allowed backdating for match. 4) payroll will calculate retro employer match if vendor permits.

michael: Thanks — employee is Priya K (priya.k@redwood.com). EOR payroll shows both employee deferrals and employer match posted to GlobalHire plan Jan–Mar. She had no 401(k) loan. Can you confirm the exact info to request from GlobalHire so we don't have to go back and forth?

sarah: Please request from GlobalHire: - full contribution history (employee/employer) as CSV - paydates & paystubs for Jan–Apr - any plan docs indicating whether contributions were pre-tax or Roth - proof of enrollment date with GlobalHire plan. Also ask for a statement showing vested %, if they maintain vesting.

ben-payroll: I'll flag payroll to reserve a retro match bucket once vendor confirms allowed backdating. If vendor denies backdating, we can still accept a rollover of employee deferrals (direct rollover to Fidelity) but employer match may need to be done prospectively per plan docs.

priya: Thanks for the ping, team. Quick Q: if the GlobalHire contributions are rolled into Fidelity, will that affect my year-to-date deferral limits or catch-up eligibility? I was age 50 in 2025 and planned catch-up contributions.

sarah: @priya good question — rolled-over amounts don't count toward the IRS annual elective deferral limit for the year of the rollover. They won't affect your ability to contribute catch-up amounts for the current year. However, employee deferrals reported by GlobalHire for payroll periods in 2025 do count as deferrals toward the 2025 limit if they were salary deferrals; we need the export to reconcile. We'll confirm with benefits team.

benefits-team: Looping in benefits. We need: 1) GlobalHire contribution report; 2) signed transfer authorization from Priya; 3) confirmation of whether EOR service should be credited for vesting (we'll need a policy decision but can escalate). If Priya wants employer match retroactively, vendor approval required.

sam: Template you can send GlobalHire (copy/paste):

```
Please provide:
- Employee full name: Priya K
- SSN last 4: XXXX
- Employment dates with GlobalHire: 2025-01-06 — 2025-04-14
- Detailed contribution history (employee/employer) with paydates and amounts, CSV preferred
- Plan name and plan document, including any employer match and vesting language
- Contact for plan admin and signed participant authorization to release records
```

michael: Perfect — I'll send that now. Any sense of timeline for confirmation? We want to close this before open enrollment prep next month. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ben-payroll: Once we have GlobalHire docs and fidelity responds, vendor turnaround is typically 7–14 business days. If we need a manual retro contribution entry, payroll will need at least one full payroll cycle + vendor processing window.

sarah: We'll triage as high priority. I'll cc benefits & payroll, and open an internal case. @priya — can you reply with the signed authorization when you have a minute? :wave:

priya: On it, sending signed form now. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:

michael: Thanks y'all — appreciate the rapid help.
